title: VPC & On‑Prem Persona Messaging Matrix and Response Scripts
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a pragmatic messaging matrix and a set of short scripts for sales/solutions/AE to use when discussing VPC and on‑prem Private deployments with regulated buyers (finance, healthcare, gov / public sector). Focus: control plane framing, data residency, auditability, and the common buyer objections we see in POCs.

Status: draft — notes from 2025‑01 customer calls, internal syncs. Use/adapt; flag anything inaccurate to @Aisha.

High‑level positioning (single line):
- For engineering and security teams that cannot put data in a third‑party shared control plane, Redwood Private provides an operationally‑managed inference runtime while giving customers a customer‑owned control plane and turnkey auditability.

Key control plane frames (short):
- Customer‑owned control plane: control plane components run in the customer VPC (or on‑prem network), credentials and keys never leave your environment, Redwood agents manage runtime inside the network.
- Managed control plane (hybrid option): minimal control plane in Redwood cloud for lifecycle operations, with certed TLS channels and optional deployable controllers for audit/hotfix rollback — used only when customer permits.
- Air‑gapped mode: full offline install with audited package manifests and signed binary bundles; required for highest regulation levels.

Persona matrix (problem → what they care about → 1‑line message → proof points / collateral to reference):
- CISO / Security architecture
  - cares: key custody, network isolation, audit trails, breach blast radius
  - message: "We run inference in your network and integrate with your KMS/HSM so keys never leave your boundary; control plane artifacts are stored in your audit systems."
  - proof: KMS/HSM integration doc + sample audit log export (Confluence link), SOC2/ISO excerpts, architecture diagram (VPC peering, private link).

- Platform/Infra Lead
  - cares: IaC, upgrades, lifecycle, automation, observability, SLOs
  - message: "We deliver Terraform modules and Helm charts, and a declarative control plane controller that you run in your cluster — upgrades are orchestrated via Canary jobs and can be pinned by version."
  - proof: GitHub repo link for helm charts, example Terraform module, runbook for upgrades.

- Legal/Privacy/Compliance
  - cares: data residency, PII processing, contracts/DPAs, auditability for regulators
  - message: "We provide contract language for data residency, support customer managed audit logs and provide exportable evidence bundles for audits — we do not access or persist customer payloads outside your infrastructure unless explicitly enabled."
  - proof: sample DPA clause, evidence package checklist, prior customer reference (anonymized).

- Procurement / Finance
  - cares: TCO, commitment model, vendor risk, termination data handling
  - message: "Private deployments are available as an enterprise license (platform + support) with optional reserved capacity; deprovisioning includes certified data wipe reports."
  - proof: pricing brief, deprovisioning certificate template.

Direct objection handling (short scripts):
- "We can’t let your vendor run a control plane in our VPC."
  - Script: "Understood — Redwood Private supports a customer‑owned control plane: the control plane services are deployed in your account (or on‑prem), we operate controllers/agents under the permissions you grant, and all secrets are stored in your KMS. We can walk your security team through the minimal IAM surface and the SOC2 excerpts that describe access controls."

- "We need guarantees that data never leaves X region / we can’t allow egress."
  - Script: "We support region‑pinned deployments and disable any outbound egress by default; for connectivity we use VPC peering/private link and do not route inference payloads outside your networks. We include a network topology diagram showing no public NAT paths in the standard package."

- "Vendor patching and urgent fixes — what access do you need?"
  - Script: "We ship signed fix bundles and a controller that can apply them; for emergency hotfixes we offer an ‘attested patch’ mode where patches are staged in your artifact repo and executed by your operators, with full runbooks and rollback. We never auto‑execute binaries without explicit operator approval in production mode."

- "How do you handle keys?"
  - Script: "We integrate with your KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Cloud HSM, Azure Key Vault, on‑prem HSM), and the inference runtime uses keys via in‑memory operations — no encryption keys are exported. We can provide the crypto attestation package for your crypto team."

Competitive callouts — quick plays (how to position vs common alternatives):
- Public cloud managed LLM APIs (simplicity vs control): 
  - Play: emphasize control plane ownership, certifiable audit bundles, and network isolation. If they require absolute simplicity and have no regulatory constraints, hosted is fine; if they require attestable controls, push Private.

- Self‑hosted open‑source stacks + ops (Flexibility vs operational load):
  - Play: acknowledge flexibility but contrast the operational burden — Redwood Private gives a hardened, tested runtime, model lifecycle tooling (rollouts, canaries, fallback), and predictable support SLAs so platform teams don’t have to build everything. Share failure‑mode stories (anonymized) if helpful.

- Appliance / vendor hardware offers (single‑vendor lock):
  - Play: highlight deployment flexibility (cloud, dedicated colo, on‑prem) and rolling upgrades without forklift hardware costs; we integrate with customer infrastructure and avoid lock‑in to a proprietary appliance.

Suggested collateral snippets (copy‑ready, short):
- For security slides: "Customer‑owned control plane + customer KMS = keys never leave your boundary. Audit log export available to your SIEM."
- For procurement brief: "Enterprise license + on‑prem packaging; includes upgrade SLA, compliance evidence kit, and deprovisioning certificate."
- For platform teams: "Terraform + Helm + Controller pattern: declarative lifecycle, canary upgrades, pinned model versions."

Sample one‑minute elevator pitches (three variants):
- Technical / platform: "Redwood Private runs inference in your network and provides terraform and helm tooling so platform teams treat models like any other service — pinned versions, canary rollouts, and audit trails. No third‑party control plane dependencies."
- Security‑first: "We give you the telemetry and control you require: control plane components run in your account, we integrate with your KMS/HSM, and audit logs are exported to your SIEM on a retention schedule you control."
- Procurement: "Private deployments combine our inference runtime with an enterprise license and turnkey integration; predictable unit economics, support SLAs, and certified deprovisioning reduce vendor risk."

Open questions / risks (items for PD/Product to resolve before wider use):
- what level of ‘managed control plane’ hybrid mode is acceptable to Legal (minimal metadata exchange)? (action: @Legal to propose acceptable metadata whitelist)
- standard contract language for HSM integrations (we need templated appendix) (owner: @Claire)
- cleanup scripts: certified data wipe template needs product sign‑off and a test plan (owner: @Omar)

Next steps / TODOs: (quick)
- Pull together a short 1‑pager with the three elevator pitches and attach to sales playbook (owner: Aisha; due 2025‑01‑22).
- Add a technical appendix with sample terraform and network diagrams (owner: Diego; due 2025‑01‑29).
- Run an internal dry run with SRE/infra and Security to validate scripts and IAM minimal surface (owner: Platform Eng; schedule week of 2025‑01‑20).

Appendix — quick links to artifacts we reference (internal):
- Signed package / airgap playbook: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/PD/Airgap+Install+Playbook
- Helm + Terraform examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/helm-charts/tree/main/private
- Sample audit evidence template (DPA appendix): https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/Legal/DPA+Evidence+Template

Notes / scraps (raw):
- Customer asked if we can do 'snapshot backups of KV cache' for reproducibility — currently storing cache snapshots for debug is opt‑in and stored in customer S3 under their account.
- Example objection we heard from large bank: 'We want zero inbound connections from vendor IPs' — response: 'All vendor operations run as outbound calls from inside your VPC to your artifact repo or to a control socket initiated by your controller.'

End of draft.
summary: Messaging matrix and objection scripts for Private (VPC/on‑prem) targeting regulated buyers; control plane framing, persona lines, proof points, competitive playbooks, and open action items.
